obligations.finding: FDLE's current public renderer has no Administrative Expunction request type. Current Florida Administrative Code Rule 11C-7.008 does not prescribe or incorporate an FDLE form: it requires an application in writing, with an agency-letterhead route or a written applicant request plus written agency or state-attorney endorsement. The assignment label is a descriptive procedure/output, not the identity of a published uniform form.
obligations.prescribedOutput: A custom written application and, when applicant-submitted, a custom written endorsement; not an FDLE application form.

obligations.identityProblem: No separate 'attached sheet' is published. Rule 2.86—Form 2 is one three-page instrument. Page 1 lets the filer check a box if the filer has attached a sheet with additional alternate names, and page 2 lets the filer check a box if the filer has attached a sheet with additional related-case information. Those are user-created continuation sheets, not an Iowa Judicial Branch form. The separately published Instructions for Rule 2.86—Form 2 are a different document and must not be substituted.
obligations.captainDecisionRequired: Remove the phantom official-form obligation and model optional user-created attachments inside Form 2, or create a clearly non-official continuation-sheet composer requirement.

fdleAcquireOnceFinding.finding: The publisher treats sealing and expunction as one FDLE40-021 instrument and the printed title covers both, but the current renderer writes the selected request type into the PDF and emits a per-render UUID. The two exact renderings are therefore not byte-identical: Expunge is sha256 ced5d88f7305780a0d2f6354eca313f32729aa25c1b6782013f8bc6847d4c650 and Seal is sha256 1d07f48487cc466294a25fd36f06fb15002d1fa524dd43889c3ddb832c1f8aec. Expunge serves fl-10yr-bridge-set and fl-expunction-set; Seal serves fl-sealing-set.
fdleAcquireOnceFinding.whyTwoRenderingsWerePreserved: One common identity was acquired from one official renderer, but exact family-ready bytes require the publisher-selected request type. Both successful official responses are preserved under the no-delete rule.
